title: align openai /v1/chat.completions role semantics, stop/logprobs and structured-response framing
author: Samaira Patel
description: Motivation: Customers expect exact parity with OpenAI's /v1/chat.completions for role handling, stop sequences, and logprobs output shape. We also have recurring streaming edgecases where role tokens arrive as separate SSE events leading to downstream SDKs mis-attributing first assistant delta. This PR harmonizes the OpenAI-compat layer to produce: 1) canonical role deltas where the initial assistant role is coalesced into the first token event; 2) explicit mapping for 'stop' as either string or array and consistent enforcement across server- and client-side truncation; 3) support for returning token-level logprobs and top_k entries when logprobs>0 is requested; 4) a structured-output framing option that injects a stable JSON wrapper event and schema hint to help SDKs auto-parse structured responses. Changes are backward-compatible by default: legacy clients keep previous behavior unless the compatibility flag openai_compat.enable_new_role_delta is enabled in config; the structured-output framing is opt-in via parameter structured_output=true. Risk/compatibility notes: the logprobs payload can be large and is gated behind both the request param and a per-tenant quota to avoid accidental cost spikes. Streaming changes required subtle buffering to coalesce role tokens; buffer size is capped and falls back to previous behavior on overflow to avoid head-of-line blocking. What this PR does: -- Introduces openai_compat role coalescing logic and deterministic SSE event order. -- Adds parsing and normalization for stop param (string|array) and validates server truncation semantics. -- Implements token-level logprobs serialization matching OpenAI shape: tokens, token_logprobs, top_logprobs (top-k as objects). -- Adds structured-output framing: emits an initial "structured_schema" SSE event with user-provided schema hint, then emits 'delta' events with content_parts tagged. -- Adds comprehensive unit and integration tests, plus an e2e replay harness against a testrpc model to validate SSE order. Testing: new unit tests in pkg/openai_compat/*, integration tests in tests/integration/openai_compat_streaming_test.go, and end-to-end recorded replay scenarios added to benchmark-lab. CI: initial flaky test in sse_emitter was fixed by adding a small deterministic backoff in the emitter; all checks green on final run. Docs: updated docs/openai_compat.md and examples with structured-output example. Rollout plan: feature gated, enabled for staged tenants during canary week; monitoring added to detect a 5xx or SSE reorder regression. Checklist: [x] role coalescing logic implemented [x] stop param normalization [x] logprobs serialization [x] structured-output framing (opt-in) [x] unit/integration/e2e tests added [x] docs updated [x] feature flag and monitoring added

review_conversation: Ava Chen: Please confirm that the coalescing avoids adding latency for small responses. Samaira Patel: We limit coalescing window to 10ms by default and fall back on overflow; latency regression tested <0.5ms p50 in microbenchmarks.

Diego Martinez: The logprobs schema looks good but clarify top_k ordering. Samaira Patel: top_logprobs is now emitted as objects mapping token->score and we added docs to clarify ordering is not guaranteed; SDKs should sort if necessary.
Priya Singh: Can we gate structured-output behind a feature flag? Samaira Patel: Yes, structured_output=true param plus a tenant-level feature flag; added monitoring for parse failures.

Oliver K. Baker: CI failed once on sse_emitter concurrency flake; resolved by deterministic backoff and a retry on non-fatal EPIPE. Samaira Patel: added tests to reproduce and fixed emitter accordingly.
Ava Chen: Approving after the docs update. (approved)
Priya Singh: Approved after a small nits patch to examples. (approved)
release_notes: Adds OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity improvements: canonical role delta coalescing, normalized stop param handling, token-level logprobs and top_logprobs mapping, and an opt-in structured-output framing for robust SDK parsing. Feature-gated and rolled out to canary tenants first.
